abstract: I theorize that candidate filters, a core technology in digital labor markets considered central to cost-effective matching, redistributes costs from the search-and-screening stage to the job-offer stage of hiring. Filters cause employers to focus on applicants who display common preferred characteristics. At the search-and-screening stage, filters reduce the number of applicants interviewed and alter the composition of the interviewed pool by removing both lower- and higher-quality candidates. At the job-offer stage, filters lead employers to make job offers to candidates with easily observable signals of quality and higher wage demands. Additionally, I theorize that if many firms target the same signals of quality, they may all pursue similar candidates. This increases bargaining power for those applicants, leading to more rejected job offers and higher wage demands. A randomized field experiment in a large online labor market confirms that filters redistribute hiring costs. The experiment shows that employers with access to filters interview 3.4% fewer applicants. Using a machine learning algorithm to proxy for unobservable-to-the-employer applicant quality, I show that filters cause employers to interview 28.9% fewer lower-quality applicants and 36.9% fewer high-quality applicants per job. Among employers who actively used filters, I find suggestive evidence of worse job-offer outcomes: offers are 8.9% more likely to be rejected, and contracted wages are 2.5% higher. I discuss the implications of this cost redistribution for organizations, labor markets, and strategy research.

ob.tldr: 理论研究数字劳动力市场中候选人筛选器如何将招聘成本从搜索与面试阶段重新分配至录用阶段。筛选器使雇主聚焦于具备共同偏好特征的应聘者，减少面试量并改变面试池构成，同时导致录用阶段雇主青睐易观察质量信号且薪资要求更高的候选人；多家企业追逐同类信号时增强应聘者议价能力。线上劳动力市场随机田野实验验证：使用筛选器的雇主面试量减少3.4%，低质量与高质量应聘者面试分别减少28.9%与36.9%，且录用被拒概率上升8.9%，合同薪资高出2.5%。

title: Filtering the labor pool: How digitalization redistributes hiring costs
title_zh: 过滤劳动力池：数字化如何重分配招聘成本
